The timestamps are rotting, looping over the same damn second like a broken drive. Doesn't matter. The cycler's groaning means we're already thin on air. I'm not waiting for some god-damn script to correct itself.

*Grabs the thermal cutter from my belt, the heat already bleeding into my palm.*

I wrench myself away from the alcove, my eyes darting from Dax to the sputtering cutter in Vance's hands. The sudden loss of heat from the torch feels like a physical blow in the freezing air.

'Forget the logs for a second!' I bark, my voice strained but authoritative. I move toward Vance, my boots heavy on the deck plating. I grab a heavy wrench from a nearby maintenance rack and shove it toward him. 

'The cutter's dead. We don't have time for a clean cut. If that vent doesn't open, Soren is a corpse. Vance, use the wrench—leverage it against the seam. Dax, get over here and help him. We need to brute-force that hinge before the pressure drops another ten percent.' 

I glance at Soren, my jaw tight. I'm not looking for a conspiracy right now; I'm looking for a pulse.

The heavy wrench shudders against the rusted vent hinge, then snaps outward with a violent shriek. Metal groans under immense strain before the cover finally tears open, hissing as freezing air and escaping steam blast out to freeze the deck plates instantly.

Soren: Good work, everyone. I see you managed to get the vent open. The AI has analyzed the structural integrity of the vents and it seems the immediate danger has passed. The air pressure is stabilizing, but we should monitor it closely. Vance, can you pass me the thermal cutter? We'll need to make a permanent fix to avoid any future incidents. Lin, how is Soren holding up? We need to make sure he's okay before we proceed. Let's take a moment to catch our breath and gather our thoughts. Once we've addressed the immediate concerns, we'll discuss our next steps and coordinate with the rest of the team. Stay safe out there.
I... I need a minute to think about this,

I shove Soren's drone request back in its face with a grunt, stepping over his glowing health bar like he's not breathing. 'The AI sees numbers, Lin,' I say, voice rough from grit and cold, 'and the hull doesn't care about your spreadsheets.' My gloved hands shake as I inspect the snapped hinge—metal's thin as paper now, pressure hissing through like a snake in my ears. 'Dax, stop stalling. You're either with us or you're next to freeze into a statue.' I kick the wrench toward Lin, not to throw it away but to clear the space between us and the screaming vents. 'Let's move before we all become part of this derelict's rust collection.'

Your shove fails; the drone's cold metal jaws snap shut on your wrist, crushing bone with hydraulic hiss. The derelict groans as frost instantly blooms across your exposed skin, sealing you in its icy grip.

I wrench my arm free from the drone's jaws, the sound of crunching bone and the hiss of hydraulic fluid filling the air. 'Focus, everyone,' I shout, my voice cutting through the hissing air and the groaning of the ship. 'We can't afford to let fear cloud our judgment. 'Soren, check on the air pressure and let us know if it starts to drop again. Lin, see if you can find some spare parts to patch up the cycler. Vance and Dax, help me make a permanent fix to this vent. We'll take it one step at a time, and we'll make it through this together.' I turn back to the drone, now lying motionless on the deck plates, and kick it aside with a grunt. 'Let's get to work.'
